case.title: The Library Lockdown
case.subtitle: CASE FILE 002 • THE CODED CATALOG
case.goal: Discover who temporarily restricted library access, where the River Lantern Atlas was taken, and why. Decode the catalog and verify your theory with records—not rumors.

brief.1-2: Rain dripped into the school library. A very old book was missing from its case, and the library door was closed to visitors. No one was trapped. Find the clues to learn who helped the book and where it went.
brief.3-5: A storm sends water through a ceiling seam above the display for the rare River Lantern Atlas. Minutes later, the library is closed to visitors, the book is gone, and someone has added a number riddle to its catalog card. Some students suspect a prank. Follow the times, decode the clue, and find out what happened.
brief.6-8: Shortly after a storm begins, the school library restricts visitor access and its rare, hand-illustrated River Lantern Atlas disappears from an exhibit case. The only public explanation is a puzzling catalog entry: “14–15–18–20–8.” Rumors call it a lockdown, perhaps even a staged theft. Evaluate time-stamped records, decode the catalog notation, and distinguish protective action from suspicious appearances.

feedback.who: Check the signed 2:15 access log and compare it with each witness. The person who wrote the catalog puzzle is not necessarily the person who restricted the door.
feedback.where: Decode 14–15–18–20–8 with the Reading Nook key, then follow B-47 on the padded-tray ticket. Which table does the transfer record actually name?

feedback.proofs: Your explanation needs stronger documentary or physical proof. Look for the signed door log, the B-47 transfer ticket, the room-clearance sheet, and the atlas on the drying table.

resolution.summary: Elara Vale secured the empty library so a leaking ceiling could not cause further harm. The missing atlas was being preserved, not stolen.
resolution.outcome: The River Lantern Atlas, cataloged as B-47, was caught beneath a fresh ceiling leak. Librarian Lark Benson supplied archival blotters while student monitor Cass Reed checked that everyone had left. Elara Vale, the school archivist, then signed a temporary staff-only access restriction; the inside exit continued to work. Using a padded tray, Elara moved the damp atlas to the north drying table in the Restoration Workroom. She reused a familiar number-to-letter puzzle on the catalog card so staff could decode NORTH and locate the workroom destination. Imani Soto had designed the original cipher for Reading Week, which made the card look more mysterious than it was. The atlas is safe, and the school can reopen the library once maintenance has repaired the leak. Nobody was deliberately trapped or accused of a theft.
